summary: The note defines heliocentrism as the astronomical model in which Earth and the planets revolve around a central Sun, and contrasts it with geocentrism, which placed Earth at the center. It notes that Aristarchus of Samos proposed Earth's revolution around the Sun as early as the 3rd century BC, but that this idea attracted little attention in the medieval world, possibly due to the loss of Hellenistic-era scientific works.
one_line: Heliocentrism is the astronomical model placing the Sun at the center of the Solar System, opposed historically to geocentrism.
key_facts: Heliocentrism is the astronomical model in which the Earth and planets revolve around the Sun at the center of the Solar System.
Historically, heliocentrism was opposed to geocentrism, which placed the Earth at the center.
The notion that the Earth revolves around the Sun had been proposed as early as the 3rd century BC.
Aristarchus of Samos proposed that the Earth revolves around the Sun as early as the 3rd century BC.
At least in the medieval world, Aristarchus's heliocentrism attracted little attention.
One possible reason heliocentrism attracted little medieval attention is the loss of scientific works of the Hellenistic Era.
